title: Tiny Snakes Cartwheel Away From Danger
paragraphs: Dwarf reed snakes are small snakes from Southeast Asia. Most are less than 30 centimetres long. Scientists have now studied how they move when they are in danger.

A team from Toho University in Japan filmed 13 snakes from a national park in Malaysia. All of them rolled across a narrow track. Six snakes of another group, which were used for comparison, never rolled.

When a snake rolls, one side of its body hits the ground, and then the other side does. This movement is about four times faster than normal sliding. Even then, the head stays steady and points forward, so the snake can see where it is going.

questions.q: Where did the 13 snakes come from?
questions.a: From a national park in Malaysia.

questions.q: Did the other six snakes roll?
Why is a steady head useful?
questions.a: The snake can see where it is going.
